extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, researchers, conference/workshop organizers, and prospective participants (faculty, postdocs, grad students)
extracted.subtask_description: Listings of mathematics conferences, workshops, and summer schools with explicit submission, registration, and participation requirements (deadlines, abstract lengths, formats, fees, selection procedures). Useful for prospective speakers, demo authors, and attendees planning submissions or applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference purpose and topical relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference themes/purpose describe which topics and audiences the meeting targets (e.g., interdisciplinary computational algebra and number theory; mathematics motivated by biological experiments; applications in algebra, coding theory, combinatorics, cryptography, design theory, DSP, hardware design, physics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed contributions (talks, posters, demos) should be relevant to the listed topics and the stated interdisciplinary goals; align abstracts with the conference themes to improve selection chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended abstract length and deadline for contributed talks
rubrics_metrics.description: For contributed talks (example: Second Magma Conference) send an extended abstract (one to three pages) for proposed contributed talks before March 8, 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program committee will select talks (selection announced by April 1). Selected speakers will be invited to submit a full paper for usual refereeing (e.g., Journal of Symbolic Computation). Follow stated page-length and deadline exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software demonstration proposal format and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers welcome submissions for the demonstration of software; send a short (one-page) proposal before March 8, 1996 (example: Magma Conference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep demo proposals to the requested length and submit by the stated deadline; proposals may be selected for software demonstrations at the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference structure and presentation formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical conference components: invited talks, contributed talks, workshops, software demonstrations, and poster sessions (explicitly listed for multiple conferences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing content, choose the format that fits your contribution (e.g., software demo vs contributed talk vs poster); organizers may allocate sessions according to these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poster sessions as overflow/alternative presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If necessary a poster session will be organized to allow additional contributions to be presented (example appears in Magma Conference listing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contributed-talk slots are limited, consider proposing a poster; mention if a poster is acceptable when submitting an abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocated talk durations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributed talks have specified time allocations (examples: 30-minute contributed talks at Magma Conference; 25 minutes per contributed talk at the Dundee Conference; plenary 40 minutes and sectional reports 20 minutes in other listings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare talks to fit the announced duration; organizers will allocate the listed time for presentation and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and post-selection publication process
rubrics_metrics.description: Program committees select contributed talks; selected speakers may be invited to submit full papers which will undergo the usual refereeing process for conference proceedings or journals (example: invited to submit to Journal of Symbolic Computation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to expand an accepted abstract into a full refereed paper; meet any further submission deadlines and formatting requirements for proceedings/journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channels and abstract publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts and application materials should be sent by the specified means (post, e-mail, or WWW) and by the stated deadlines; some conferences will publish abstracts or proceedings after the meeting (examples: applications/abstracts sent by post or e-mail; conference proceedings to be published/refereed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated submission channel (include requested contact/address) and include any required elements (abstract length, title, author info) to ensure consideration and inclusion in published materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑registration / application form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some conferences require pre-registration with specific fields (example INPRIM-96 pre-registration: 1. First name 2. Middle name 3. Last name 4. Position 5. Address 6. Fax 7. Phone 8. E-mail 9. Title and one page abstract of the talk 10. Date of birth 11. Nationality (Citizenship) 12. Passport number 13. Remarks and wishes 14. Data for accompanying persons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all requested information in the pre-registration to avoid delays or denial of participation; include the one-page abstract when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and target audience for specific workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops and NSF-funded projects may specify eligible applicants (example: ATLAST workshops invite all teachers of undergraduate linear algebra courses at colleges or universities in the USA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm eligibility before applying; tailor applications to meet program aims (e.g., teachers designing classroom lessons) and include any required supporting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant limits, screening, and notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Some workshops are limited in size (example: ATLAST workshops limited to thirty participants). A screening committee will review applications and notify applicants by a stated date (example: decisions by the beginning of April).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply by deadline and provide complete application materials; be aware that late applications may be accepted only on a space-available basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late application / space-available policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Late applications will be accepted on a space-available basis (explicitly stated for some workshops such as ATLAST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit by the primary deadline if possible; if late, contact organizers to check space availability rather than assuming acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration fees, payment procedures, and first-come policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Some short courses require payment to secure a place (example: Calculus enhanced with computer-algebra: applicants accepted on a first-come first-served basis upon receipt of the $150 registration fee; payment instructions and check payee included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required payment promptly and follow the stated payee and mailing instructions to guarantee registration; watch for conference rates and hotel information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants, financial support, and fee waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain programs may offer grants covering registration or partial support (example: CRM can offer a limited number of grants covering the registration fee for Advanced Courses — deadlines apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply for grants by the stated date and include any required justification or documentation; do not assume support unless explicitly awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure and expected participant activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops and summer schools specify program formats and participant activities (examples: combination of integrated lectures and computer laboratories/demonstrations, exercises in numerical computation and data analysis, problem sessions, expository talks, seminars; participants may design classroom lessons and computer exercises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect active participation (labs, problem sessions, exercise design) when attending; prepare in advance if exercises or software demonstrations are part of the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation languages and session types
rubrics_metrics.description: Some meetings state official languages and the mix of session types (example: International Research Conference lists official languages: English, Russian; program includes plenary reports, sectional reports, poster reports, round-table talks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your presentation and materials are prepared in an accepted language and fit the declared session type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration inclusions and accommodation options
rubrics_metrics.description: Some meetings specify what registration covers and accommodation arrangements (example: summer school fee includes full board with three meals a day, lodging, excursion; accommodation in single/double rooms; round-trip bus fare listed separately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check what the fee includes and budget for additional travel or local transport costs; follow stated payment deadlines for registration and accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference-specific deadlines and contact procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listing provides precise deadlines for abstracts, applications, registration, and instructions for contacting organizers (mailing addresses, telephone, fax, and e-mail; some provide WWW pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to each conference's specified deadlines and use the provided contact method(s); consult the listed WWW or e‑mail contacts for updates or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings and refereed publications policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Several conferences indicate that proceedings (sometimes refereed) will be published after the meeting (example: refereed Conference Proceedings for the Geoffrey J. Butler Memorial Conference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your contribution is accepted, be prepared to submit a full paper as required for inclusion in published proceedings and to meet the editors' formatting and deadlines.
